rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows people's inward intentions, deeds, and speech, and treats them according to what He knows.
rows.anchor: يعلم ما يضمره الناس وما يعملونه ويعلم ما ينطقون به فهو يعاملهم بما يعلم منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning God as Hearing before Knowing hints that the change involved the rejecters' words, their invocation of deities besides God.
rows.anchor: يومىء إلى أن التغيير الذي أحدثه المعرض بهم متعلق بأقوالهم وهو دعوتهم آلهة غير الله تعالى

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqatil's anomalous report says the final two verses of the surah are Meccan.
rows.anchor: ما روي عن مقاتل : أن آيتين من آخرها مكيتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says 9:19 came down about al-Abbas after his capture at Badr, when Ali reproached him for unbelief and severed kinship.
rows.anchor: أجعلتم سقاية الحاج } ( التوبة : 19 ) الآية . نزل في العباس إذ أسر يوم بدر فعيره علي بن أبي طالب بالكفر

rows.speaker: الجميع
rows.claim: All agree this is the last surah revealed; Jaber ibn Zayd dates it after al-Fath, making it the 114th in revelation order.
rows.anchor: آخر السور نزولا عند الجميع ، نزلت بعد سورة الفتح ، في قول جابر بن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports place its revelation in early Shawwal or late Dhu al-Qada of year nine, after or just before Abu Bakr left for pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: نزلت في أول شوال سنة تسع ، وقيل آخر ذي القعدة سنة تسع ، بعد خروج أبي بكر الصديق من المدينة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority hold that the surah was revealed all at once, like Surat al-Anam among the long surahs.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على أنها نزلت دفعة واحدة ، فتكون مثل سورة الأنعام بين السور الطوال

rows.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
rows.claim: Many commentators interpret some verses as having been revealed in separated episodes over extended periods.
rows.anchor: وفسر كثير من المفسرين بعض آيات هذه السورة بما يقتضي أنها نزلت أوزاعا في أوقات متباعدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He suggests that saying the surah was not revealed piecemeal may mean no other surah began to be revealed in between.
rows.anchor: ولعل مراد من قال إنها نزلت غير متفرقة : أنه يعني إنها لم يتخللها ابتداء نزول سورة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He considers it likely that the first thirteen verses were revealed consecutively, as the reports about Ali announcing them at the pilgrimage agree.
rows.anchor: نزلت متتابعة ، كما سيأتي في خبر بعث علي بن أبي طالب ليؤذن بها في الموسم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported view says the first thirty verses, through 9:30, were announced at the pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: أذن بها يوم الموسم ، وقيل : أربعين آية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported view says forty verses, through 9:40, were announced at the pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: أذن به في الموسم ، كما سيأتي أيضا في مختلف الروايات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reconciling the reports, he thinks forty verses were probably revealed consecutively, while allowing that the whole surah may have come at once.
rows.anchor: فالجمع بينها يغلب الظن بأن أربعين آية نزلت متتابعة ، على أن نزول جميع السورة دفعة واحدة ليس ببعيد عن الصحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After severity toward disbelievers and criticism of negligent believers, the surah praises emigrants, supporters, and those who followed the Messenger in hardship.
rows.anchor: وتخلل ذلك تنويه بالمتصفين بضد ذلك من المؤمنين الذين هاجروا والذين نصروا واتبعوا الرسول في ساعة العسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final two verses recall the blessing of Muhammad's mission and praise his complete virtues, especially his desire for people's guidance, faith, and entry into Islam.
rows.anchor: والتنويه بصفاته الجامعة للكمال . ومن أخصها حرصه على هداهم ، ورغبته في إيمانهم ودخولهم في جامعة الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harsh treatment of those turning from Islam aims to reform them and is itself a form of the mercy accompanying the Messenger's mission.
rows.anchor: ما هو إلا استصلاح لحالهم . وهذا من مظاهر الرحمة التي جعلها الله تعالى مقارنة لبعثة رسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses answer earlier severity with gentleness and mercy, opening the way of faith and repentance to those God guides.
rows.anchor: تعقيبا للشدة بالرفق وللغلظة بالرحمة ، وكذلك عادة القرآن . فقد انفتح بهاتين الآيتين باب حظيرة الإيمان والتوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence begins a new discourse, and its position at the surah's end gives it the force of a concluding summary.
rows.anchor: فالجملة مستأنفة استئنافا ابتدائيا . وفي وقوعها آخر السورة ما يكسبها معنى التذييل والخلاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address encompasses the whole community invited to Islam, but its immediate primary audience is Arab polytheists and hypocrites, as the following description indicates.
rows.anchor: موجه إلى جميع الأمة المدعوة للإسلام . والمقصود بالخطاب بادىء ذي بدء هم المعرضون من المشركين والمنافقين من العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lam and qad intensify the opening to stress its important purpose, answer hypocrites who deny the Messenger's divine commission, and treat the audience as deniers because they failed to benefit from his coming.
rows.anchor: وافتتاحها بحرفي التأكيد وهما اللام و ( قد ) مع كون مضمونها مما لا يتطرق إليه الإنكار لقصد الاهتمام بهذه الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the already familiar fact that the Messenger came implicitly signals that his departure is near and records this for believers, hypocrites, and remaining polytheists.
rows.anchor: به الإيماء إلى اقتراب الرحيل ، لأنه لما أعيد الإخبار بمجيئه وهو حاصل منذ أعوام طويلة كان ذلك كناية عن اقتراب انتهائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stronger emphasis here has a more urgent purpose than the lesser emphasis in addresses to the People of the Book and all people.
rows.anchor: على أن آيات أخرى خوطب بها أهل الكتاب ونحوهم فأكدت بأقل من هذا التأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger's coming is a metaphor for addressing people with the invitation to religion, like an unexpected visitor; this usage is common in the Quran.
rows.anchor: وهو استعمال شائع في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anfus means selves, and when attached to a pronoun denotes the tribe to which it refers; here it means the Messenger belonged to the Arabs' core lineage, not through alliance or clientage.
rows.anchor: أي هو معدود من ذوي نسبهم وليس عداده فيهم بحلف أو ولاء أو إلصاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means he was from the Arabs' own ancestry, since they did not count allied or client non-Arabs such as Salman and Bilal as their own; this honors them and urges them to follow him and stop opposing him.
rows.anchor: من صميم نسبكم ، فتعين أن الخطاب للعرب لأن النازل بينهم القرآن يومئذ لا يعدون العرب ومن حالفهم وتولاهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His Arab lineage is an appeal for them to take pride in him and rally around him, as the Quran will preserve an honorable remembrance for him and his people.
rows.anchor: وفيه أيضا تعريض بتحريضهم على اتباعه وترك مناواته وأن الأجدر بهم الافتخار به والالتفاف حوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aziz means prevailing; when used with ala, it conveys something heavy and distressing to the person affected.
rows.anchor: فإذا عدي بعلى دل على معنى الثقل والشدة على النفس

rows.speaker: بشر بن عوانة
rows.claim: Bishr ibn Awana's verse uses yaizz alayya to mean that it grieves him to have killed his kinsman by force.
rows.anchor: قال بشر بن عوانة في ذكر قتله الأسد ومصارعته إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma is a verbal noun particle, and anittum means you suffered or wearied; the Messenger grieves over their distress and hardship.
rows.anchor: و { ما } مصدرية . و { عنتم } : تعبتم . والعنت : التعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression recalls the Prophet nearly consuming himself with grief that people were not believers; this trait produces gentleness and care to protect the community from punishment in both lives.
rows.anchor: وذكر هذا في صفة الرسول عليه السلام يفيد أن هذا خلق له فيكون أثر ظهوره الرفق بالأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One effect of his concern is his intercession for all people at the Gathering to hasten the reckoning.
rows.anchor: ومن آثار ذلك شفاعته للناس كلهم في الموقف لتعجيل الحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The law suits the Messenger's merciful character and therefore contains no hardship.
rows.anchor: ثم إن ذلك يومىء إلى أن شرعه جاء مناسبا لخلقه فانتفى عنه الحرج والعسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using the verb with ma instead of a bare verbal noun specifies distress that actually occurred in the past, including killings, captivity, and Quranic threats; a bare verbal noun has no tense.
rows.anchor: إلى الإتيان بالفعل مع ( ما ) المصدرية السابكة للمصدر نكتة . وهي إفادة أنه قد عز عليه عنتهم الحاصل في الزمن الذي مضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This wording hints that the past hardships were intended to reform them, so that they might moderate their excess and abandon error.
rows.anchor: لتكون هذه الآية تنبيها على أن ما لقوه من الشدة إنما هو لاستصلاح حالهم لعلهم يخفضون بعدها من غلوائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hirs means intense desire; since the object cannot be the people themselves, context implies a complement such as their faith or guidance.
rows.anchor: والحرص : شدة الرغبة في الشيء والجشع إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ra'uf and rahim are intensive forms and jointly govern the phrase bil-muminin.
rows.anchor: والرؤوف : الشديد الرأفة . والرحيم : الشديد الرحمة ، لأنهما صيغتا مبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ra'fa is tenderness arising when harm befalls its recipient, while rahma entails doing good; the two overlap but differ in implications, so both are used.
rows.anchor: والرحمة : رقة تقتضي الإحسان للمرحوم ، بينهما عموم وخصوص مطلق ، ولذلك جمع بينهما هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran previously paired the divine description Ra'uf Rahim at 2:143 and mentioned mercy in the Fatiha.
rows.anchor: وتقدمت الرأفة عند قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting bil-muminin before both predicates gives special prominence to believers as recipients of the Prophet's compassion.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المتعلق على عامليه المتنازعينه في قوله : بالمؤمنين رءوف رحيم } للاهتمام بالمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His general mercy toward all creation is mixed with severity toward unbelievers; he is merciful to them but not described as ra'uf and rahim toward them.
rows.anchor: فهي رحمة مشوبة بشدة على غير المؤمنين فهو بالنسبة لغير المؤمنين رائف وراحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God their Lord rather than using the proper name honors believers and presents their guidance as a complete gift from their patron, joined with mercy and dignity.
rows.anchor: تنويه بشأن المؤمنين وشأن هدايتهم بأنها جعل مولى لأوليائه فشأنها أن تكون عطية كاملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present tense indicates that their guidance is continually renewed and their souls are prepared in worldly life to ascend in perfection.
rows.anchor: والإتيان بالمضارع للدلالة على أن هذه الهداية لا تزال متكررة متجددة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gardens and rivers clause is a second predicate describing their afterlife bliss, gained through worldly guidance; the same image appears at 2:25 and lasting bliss at 9:21.
rows.anchor: خبر ثان لذكر ما يحصل لهم من النعيم في الآخرة بسبب هدايتهم الحاصلة لهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about their call in Paradise and what follows is circumstantial of the believers.
rows.anchor: وما عطف عليها أحوال من ضمير { الذين آمنوا } .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dawa here means supplication; it can be spelled with the feminine alif or with ta marbuta.
rows.anchor: والدعوى : هنا الدعاء . يقال : دعوة بالهاء ، ودعوى بألف التأنيث .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subhan is a verbal noun meaning declaring transcendence, previously discussed at 2:32.
rows.anchor: وسبحان : مصدر بمعنى التسبيح ، أي التنزيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allahumma is a vocative to God; calling this tasbih a supplication is justified because it directly addresses God to declare His transcendence.
rows.anchor: نداء لله تعالى ، فيكون إطلاق الدعاء على هذا التسبيح من أجل أنه أريد به خطاب الله لإنشاء تنزيهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, tasbih is called supplication because praise seeks the outpouring of mercy and bliss, as in Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt's verse.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون تسمية هذا التسبيح دعاء من حيث إنه ثناء مسوق للتعرض إلى إفاضة الرحمات والنعيم

rows.speaker: أمية بن أبي الصلت
rows.claim: Umayya's verse says that praising someone can suffice instead of making a direct request.
rows.anchor: قال أمية بن أبي الصلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Limiting their opening call to Subhanaka Allahumma suggests contextual exclusivity, though not a formal restriction device; the final praise shows it too is part of their call, so they have an opening and a concluding invocation.
rows.anchor: يشعر بأنهم لا دعوى لهم في الجنة غير ذلك القول ، لأن الاقتصار في مقام البيان يشعر بالقصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salam as a greeting conveys honor and invokes safety from every disturbing thing, exceeding a wish for life alone, which might not be pleasant.
rows.anchor: إذ هو دعاء بالسلامة من كل ما يكدر ، فهو أبلغ من أحياك الله لأنه دعاء بالحياة وقد لا تكون طيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding their greeting to their pronoun means the greeting they give one another.
rows.anchor: معناها التحية التي تصدر منهم ، أي من بعضهم لبعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning their greetings signals their fellowship and joy, among the greatest pleasures of the soul.
rows.anchor: الإشارة إلى أنهم في أنس وحبور ، وذلك من أعظم لذات النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final-call clause continues the circumstantial clauses, and explanatory an makes God's praise the last phrase of their call.
rows.anchor: وجملة { وآخر دعواهم } بقية الجمل الحالية . وجعل حمد الله من دعائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They conclude their invocation with praise when moving into another state of bliss, after repeatedly saying Subhanaka Allahumma.
rows.anchor: فإذا أرادوا الانتقال إلى حالة أخرى من أحوال النعيم نهوا دعاءهم بجملة { الحمد لله رب العالمين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence suggests collective worship: they begin with tasbih upon seeing one another, exchange greetings as they approach, and end in praise when parting.
rows.anchor: فإذا اقترب بعضهم من بعض سلم بعضهم على بعض . ثم إذا راموا الافتراق ختموا دعاءهم بالحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Explanatory an indicates that the final invocation is the very phrase al-hamdu lillahi rabb al-alamin.
rows.anchor: فأن تفسيرية لآخر دعواهم ، وهي مؤذنة بأن آخر الدعاء هو نفس الكلمة { الحمد لله رب العالمين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet said that two phrases beloved to the Merciful are easy on the tongue and heavy on the scales: Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi and Subhan Allah al-Azim.
rows.anchor: قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( كلمتان حبيبتان إلى الرحمن خفيفتان على اللسان ثقيلتان في الميزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hatta marks the endpoint of building the ark; idha is conditional and its answer is We said carry, so the endpoint is realized with the response in a compact construction.
rows.anchor: { حتى } غاية ل { يصنع الفلك } ( هود : 38 ) أي يصنعه إلى زمن مجيء أمرنا ، ف { إذا } ظرف مضمن معنى الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hatta here is resumptive.
rows.anchor: و { حتى } ابتدائية . والأمر هنا يحتمل أمر التكوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command may mean God's decree bringing the flood or the event of drowning; its attribution to God magnifies it as beyond what people know.
rows.anchor: والأمر هنا يحتمل أمر التكوين بالطوفان ، ويحتمل الشأن وهو حادث الغرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command's coming means its occurrence; fawara is a pot boiling or water surging like a boiling pot.
rows.anchor: ومجيء الأمر : حصوله . والفوران : غليان القدر ، ويطلق على نبع الماء بشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other Quranic descriptions make the water eruption clear, but connecting it to a bread oven puzzled commentators and led to many interpretations, some unacceptable and others plausible.
rows.anchor: مثل قوله : { وفجرنا الأرض عيونا } ( القمر : 12 ) . ولذلك لم يتضح لهم إسناده إلى التنور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes retain the literal oven: water burst from one of Nuh's ovens as God's sign to start boarding the ark.
rows.anchor: فمن المفسرين من أبقى التنور على حقيقته ، فجعل الغوران خروج الماء من أحد التنانير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others take tannur metaphorically as the earth's surface, with all the water rising to it like the mouth of an oven.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من حمل التنور على المجاز المفرد ففسره بسطح الأرض ، أي فار الماء من جميع الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes tannur the high or highest part of the earth.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من فسره بأعلى الأرض .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others keep both words literal but read the phrase as a figure for crisis reaching its height, as in the idiom hami al-watis; the cited poem follows in the next segment.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من حمل { فار } و { التنور } على الحقيقة ، وأخرج الكلام مخرج التمثيل لاشتداد الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem means by the pot a war, and naftha means to calm it; the author calls this the best transmitted interpretation.
rows.anchor: يريد بالقدر الحرب ، ونفثأها ، أي نسكنها ، يقال : فثأ القدر إذا سكن غليانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads the phrase as a metaphor for reaching the utmost limit, like a flood reaching the hilltops, a filled measure, or an overflowing cup.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر لي أن قوله : { وفار التنور } مثل لبلوغ الشيء إلى أقصى ما يتحمل مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tannur here means a valley's gathering place or bank, making the image like a flood reaching its limit.
rows.anchor: والتنور : محفل الوادي ، أي ضفته ، فيكون مثل طما الوادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metaphor means God's decree against the people had reached its limit after prolonged disbelief, so their punishment could no longer be deferred.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : بأن نفاذ أمرنا فيهم وبلغوا من طول مدة الكفر مبلغا لا يغتفر لهم بعد

rows.speaker: ليث
rows.claim: Layth says tannur is a name for a bread oven shared among languages, like sabun and samur.
rows.anchor: وزعمه . الليث مما اتفقت فيه اللغات ، أي كالصابون والسمور

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafaji attributes to Ibn Abbas the claim that tannur is shared among languages.
rows.anchor: ونسب الخفاجي في شفاء الغليل هذا إلى ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Mansur infers from Layth's wording that tannur was originally a foreign word.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو منصور : كلام الليث يدل على أنه في الأصل أعجمي

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu Ali says tannur has the form faul; its Arabic origin is disputed because tanar is unattested and nun before ra is otherwise absent, while narjis is also borrowed.
rows.anchor: والدليل على ذلك أنه فعول من تنر ولا نعرف تنر في كلام العرب لأنه مهمل

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: Thalab argues tannur is Arabic, deriving it as taful from nur through sound changes and consonant doubling.
rows.anchor: وعن ثعلب أنه عربي ، قال : وزنه تفعول من النور

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read min kulli zawjayni with kulli in a genitive construction; a pair means male and female of every species.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { من كل زوجين } بإضافة { كل } إلى { زوجين } . والزوج : شيء يكون ثانيا لآخر في حالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is partitive and ithnayn is the object of carry; it clarifies that a pair means both members, and no species should exceed two to avoid burdening the ark.
rows.anchor: و { من } تبعيضية ، و { اثنين } مفعول { احمل } ، وهو بيان لئلا يتوهم أن يحمل كل زوجين واحدا منهما

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Hafs reads kullin with nunation as compensation for an omitted genitive; zawjayni is the object and ithnayn limits the load to two.
rows.anchor: وقرأه حفص { من كل } بتنوين { كل } فيكون تنوين عوض عن مضاف إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahl means a man's kin or household and is a collective noun without a singular; it can also mean his wife, as in the cited examples.
rows.anchor: وأهل الرجل قرابته وأهل بيته وهو اسم جمع لا واحد له . وزوجه أول من يبادر من اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those on whom the word had already passed are disbelieving members of Nuh's household under God's warning; the source identifies his wife and son and says he had two wives.
rows.anchor: و { من سبق عليه القول } أي من مضى قول الله عليه ، أي وعيده . فالتعريف في { القول } للعهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition ala after sabaqa incorporates the sense of judgment; in 37:171 the verb instead takes li because it incorporates a favorable commitment.
rows.anchor: وعدي { سبق } بحرف { على } لتضمين { سبق } معنى : حكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min amana means all believers.
rows.anchor: و { من آمن } كل المؤمنين .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause saying only a few believed is parenthetical, completing the story's point about the scarcity of the righteous.
rows.anchor: وجملة { وما آمن معه إلا قليل } اعتراض لتكميل الفائدة من القصة في قلة الصالحين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One report says Nuh's believers, family and others, numbered just over seventy men and women, while animals made up most of the ark's cargo.
rows.anchor: قيل : كان جميع المؤمنين به من أهله وغيرهم نيفا وسبعين بين رجال ونساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to board is attached to God's order to carry them; Nuh then addresses the people he was ordered to take aboard.
rows.anchor: عطف على جملة { قلنا احمل فيها } ( هود : 40 ) أي قلنا له ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fiha refers implicitly to the ship, as in the description of the ark as a vessel of planks and nails.
rows.anchor: وضمير { فيها } لمفهوم من المقام ، أي السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Riding an animal takes ala, while boarding a ship takes fi because ship-riding is metaphorical: passengers sit and settle inside it.
rows.anchor: وعدي فعل { اركبوا } ب ( في ) جريا على الفصيح فإنه يقال : ركب الدابة إذا علاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ba in bismillah marks accompaniment and is circumstantial of the addressees: they board while invoking God's name.
rows.anchor: والباء في { باسم الله } للملابسة مثل ما تقدم في تفسير البسملة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority pronounce the first vowel of both majraha and marsaha with damma; both are verbal nouns for making the ship sail and bringing it to rest.
rows.anchor: و { مجراها ومرساها } بضم الميمين فيهما في قراءة الجمهور

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم وخلف
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai, Hafs from Asim, and Khalaf read majraha with fatha as a verbal noun or time or place noun; marsaha remains with damma to avoid confusion with a mooring place.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة ، والكسائي ، وحفص عن عاصم ، وخلف ( مجراها ) فقط بفتح الميم على أنه مفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Majraha and marsaha may function as accusative time adverbs, or as nominative subjects licensed by the prepositional phrase's verbal force, a plausible Kufan analysis.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { مجراها ومرساها } في محل نصب بالنيابة عن ظرف الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuh's assurance that God is forgiving and merciful explains boarding with God's name and hints that God promised their rescue; emphatic particles reassure his followers.
rows.anchor: وجملة { إن ربي لغفور رحيم } تعليل للأمر بالركوب المقيد بالملابسة لذكر اسم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of the ship surging in mountain-like waves is parenthetical, completing the mention of its sailing and showing the day's grandeur and God's wondrous rescue.
rows.anchor: جملة معترضة دعا إلى اعتراضها هنا ذكر ( مجراها ) إتماما للفائدة وصفا لعظم اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting the subject before the verbal predicate strengthens and confirms the statement.
rows.anchor: وقدم المسند إليه على الخبر الفعلي لتقوي الحكم وتحقيقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from past tense to present conjures the scene vividly, as in the cited description of winds stirring a cloud.
rows.anchor: وعدل عن الفعل الماضي إلى المضارع لاستحضار الحالة مثل قوله تعالى : { والله الذي أرسل الرياح فتثير سحابا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawj is water rising as it moves; the waves were mountain-sized from strong winds or successive floods meeting earlier water, with earthquakes, springs, and heavy rain covering the intended land.
rows.anchor: والموج : ما يرتفع من الماء على سطحه عند اضطرابه ، وتشبيهه بالجبال في ضخامته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuh's call to his son occurred before the ark began moving, since it could not be stopped once underway and everyone had settled inside.
rows.anchor: عطفت جملة { ونادى } على أعلق الجمل بها اتصالا وهي { وقال اركبوا فيها } ( هود : 41 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The son was Nuh's fourth child by his second wife Wa'ila, who drowned and is identified with the wife in Surat al-Tahrim.
rows.anchor: وابن نوح هذا هو ابن رابع في أبنائه من زوج ثانية لنوح كان اسمها ( واعلة ) غرقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The son is variously named Yama or Canaan; he is not Canaan son of Ham, ancestor of the Canaanites.
rows.anchor: قيل كان اسم ابنه ( ياما ) وقيل اسمه ( كنعان ) وهو غير كنعان بن حام جد الكنعانيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extant Torah omits this son, his drowning, and whether he had a wife or was unmarried.
rows.anchor: وقد أهملت التوراة الموجودة الآن ذكر هذا الابن وقضية غرقه وهل كان ذا زوجة أو كان عزبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maazil means a place of separation; the son was either an unbeliever who never accepted Nuh or an apostate who denied the flood and thereby disbelieved by accusing the Messenger of falsehood.
rows.anchor: والمعزل : مكان العزلة أي الانفراد ، أي في معزل عن المؤمنين إما لأنه كان لم يؤمن بنوح عليه السلام
